narrative: Ren stood at the edge of the training grounds, his chest heaving as his sword trembled in his grip—not from physical exhaustion, but from a desperate longing to win and an intense fear of defeat. Every strike he threw was burdened by his obsession with glory and his hatred for failure. Observing from the shade of an old willow sat his master, utterly untroubled, moving with the quiet grace of a still lake. The master harbored no craving for praise nor resentment toward hardship; he was entirely free from both desire and aversion. When Ren lunged in frustration, the master effortlessly stepped aside, leaving Ren in a sudden moment of profound stillness. In that quiet pause, Ren understood: his pain did not come from the battle itself, but from his own clinging to wants and fears. By aligning his heart with the master’s unshakeable peace, the knot of anxiety in his chest unraveled. In our modern life, we too chain ourselves to endless cravings and bitter dislikes, suffering with every shifting outcome. By anchoring our spirit to the state of absolute neutrality and detachment, we shield ourselves from sorrow wherever we go.
takeaway: Anchor your soul to total equanimity, and sorrow will find no place to land.
